extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and formal requirements for preparing and filing U.S. nonprovisional and provisional patent applications (content, arrangement, filing-date rules, IDS handling, drawings, oath/fees, and related procedural requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application content (nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete application filed under § 1.53(b) or § 1.53(d) comprises: (1) A specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112, including a claim or claims (see §§ 1.71 to 1.77); (2) An oath or declaration (see §§ 1.63 and 1.68); (3) Drawings, when necessary (see §§ 1.81 to 1.85); and (4) The prescribed filing fee, search fee, examination fee, and application size fee (see § 1.16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet these requirements will result in the application being denied a filing date; the filing date is the date on which all of these requirements are met. No new matter may be introduced after the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete provisional application content
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete provisional application filed under § 1.53(c) comprises: (1) A cover sheet identifying (i) that it is a provisional application, (ii) name(s) and residence(s) of inventor(s), (iii) title of the invention, (iv) attorney/agent name and registration number (if applicable), (v) docket number (if applicable), (vi) correspondence address, (vii) name of U.S. Government agency and contract number if federally funded; (2) A specification as prescribed by the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112; (3) Drawings, when necessary; and (4) The prescribed filing fee and application size fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional application does not require claims or an oath/declaration, and an information disclosure statement (IDS) may not be filed in a provisional application. See MPEP § 201.04(b) for a sample cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements for nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a nonprovisional application under § 1.53(b) is the date on which a specification containing a description pursuant to § 1.71 and at least one claim pursuant to § 1.75, and any drawing required by § 1.81(a), are filed in the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application does not meet these requirements it will be denied a filing date; no amendment may introduce new matter after the filing date. Certain required parts (fees, oath) may be submitted later within permitted periods (see completion subsequent to filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a provisional application under § 1.53(c) is the date on which a specification as prescribed by the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 and any drawing required by § 1.81(a) are filed in the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional must include the required cover sheet (§ 1.51(c)(1)) to be treated as provisional; omission may cause it to be treated as a nonprovisional. Provisional applications are abandoned 12 months after filing unless converted or used as the basis for a later nonprovisional filing under 35 U.S.C. 119(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter after filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment that would introduce new matter is impermissible; continuing applications must follow the restrictions appropriate to their filing basis (e.g., continuation-in-part may add new matter; continuation/divisional may not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion subsequent to filing — payment of fees and oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing fee, search fee, examination fee, and an oath or declaration may be submitted after the filing date within prescribed periods and under specified conditions (including payment of a surcharge); failure to submit required fees/oath within the prescribed period will cause the application to be regarded as abandoned unless delay is shown to be unavoidable or unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant provided a correspondence address they will be notified and given time to correct; if no correspondence address was provided, applicant has two months from the filing date to supply missing items. Excess claims/multiple dependent claim fees and application size fees must be paid when due or the claims canceled prior to the reply deadline to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of incomplete filings and correction periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application does not meet filing-date requirements, applicant will be notified (if correspondence address provided) and given a period to correct the filing error; failure to correct will result in termination/abandonment and possible refund of fees less handling fee unless a timely petition (with fee) is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under § 1.17(f) is required to request review of a notification; absence of timely petition means the filing date will be the date the error is corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between provisional and nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application may be converted to a nonprovisional application and accorded the original filing date of the provisional, if conversion is requested and accompanied by the required fee and an amendment including at least one claim (unless the provisional already contains a claim). Conversely, a nonprovisional may be converted to a provisional under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion of a provisional to a nonprovisional will not result in refund of fees and may have adverse patent term impact (the term of any patent to issue from the conversion will be measured from at least the provisional filing date). Applicants are advised to consider claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) rather than converting to avoid patent-term impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution application (CPA) and continuation/divisional filing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Under § 1.53(d) a continuation or divisional (but not CIP) of a prior nonprovisional application may be filed as a continued prosecution application for design applications only; the CPA must disclose and claim only subject matter disclosed in the prior application and name the same or fewer inventors. The filing date for a CPA is the date a request on a separate paper is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs are limited in scope (design-only after certain dates). Applications under this paragraph utilize the file jacket and contents of the prior application and are assigned the prior application number for identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and required sections of the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred order of arrangement (each lettered item should appear in uppercase): (A) Title of the invention; (B) Cross-reference to related applications; (C) Statement regarding federally sponsored research or development; (D) Names of parties to joint research agreement; (E) Reference to sequence listing/table/computer program listing appendix; (F) Background of the invention (field and description of related art); (G) Brief summary of the invention; (H) Brief description of the several views of the drawing; (I) Detailed description of the invention; (J) Claims (commencing on a separate sheet); (K) Abstract of the Disclosure (commencing on a separate sheet); (L) Sequence listing, if on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This order is preferable but suggested for applicant’s use; headings should be upper case without underlining or bold type. See MPEP § 608.01(a) for paper requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and heading style
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the lettered specification items should appear in upper case, without underlining or bold type, as section headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent formatting helps examination and processing; if using an application data sheet (ADS), data need not be repeated elsewhere except for inventor citizenship in the oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) precedence and inventor/citizenship rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) is used, data supplied in the ADS need not be provided elsewhere; if there is a discrepancy between information in the ADS and elsewhere in the application, the ADS will control except for the naming of the inventors and the citizenship of the inventors (citizenship must be provided in the oath/declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency; naming and citizenship have special treatment and must be correctly stated in oath/declaration even if ADS lists them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims placement and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should commence on a separate sheet; a nonprovisional application must include at least one claim as prescribed by the second paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112. Provisional applications are not required to include claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering, dependent claims, multiple dependent claims, and form of claims are governed by MPEP § 608.01(i)-(p) and relevant CFR provisions; excess or multiple dependent claim fees must be paid as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — when required and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are required as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 113 and 37 CFR 1.81–1.85 when necessary for understanding the invention. Examiners determine the completeness and consistency of drawings; replacement drawings may be required before examination; modifications, corrections, and transfer rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are detailed MPEP provisions on acceptable drawing formats, informal drawings, replacement/correction procedures, and when annotated sheets are required. Drawing prints are kept in the file wrapper; certain drawing changes require applicant-annotated sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) — encouragement and provisional exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to file an IDS in nonprovisional applications (see §§ 1.97 and 1.98). No information disclosure statement may be filed in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since no substantive examination is made of a provisional, IDSs are unnecessary and will be returned or disposed of. For nonprovisional IDSs, strict content and timing rules apply (see MPEP § 609).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS content and timing compliance (37 CFR 1.97 & 1.98)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must comply with the content requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 and the timing requirements of 37 CFR 1.98 to be processed as an IDS; items must be listed on a separate paper and comply with form requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IDS item fails to comply it will be lined through and not considered; compliant items will be initialed by the examiner and considered. Timing affects whether a fee is required and how the IDS is processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling and marking of IDS citations
rubrics_metrics.description: When an IDS is considered the examiner must indicate which citations have been considered by marking/initialing form PTO/SB/08A and 08B (or electronic equivalent) and must fill in name and date. Citations not considered are lined through. A copy of the reviewed form is returned to the applicant and the original is entered into the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For e-IDS the examiner must electronically initial/sign and send a copy to applicant; considered citations will also be printed on the patent if format permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic IDS (e-IDS) submission rules and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: IDSs may be submitted electronically via EFS-Web. As of specified dates, an e-IDS may include citations of U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patent documents, and non-patent literature; copies of foreign/NPL/unpublished US app documents must be submitted in PDF. An individual e-IDS may contain up to combined totals (e.g., 50 U.S. patents/publications, 50 foreign patent documents, 50 NPLs) but multiple e-IDS submissions are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one e-IDS is used and a fee under § 1.17(p) is required, only a single fee may be required if (A) fee included with first e-IDS, (B) subsequent submissions state the fee was included earlier and request acceptance, and (C) all submissions are received by the Office on the same date. Applicants need not submit copies of U.S. patents and US patent application publications cited on e-IDS; examiners electronically retrieve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic annotation and examiner electronic signature for IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners use an Annotation Tool (e.g., eDAN) to electronically annotate citations and sign the IDS. Annotation applies initials to citations considered and strikes through citations not considered. Alternative electronic signature permits stamping each page with "All references considered except where lined through" plus electronic initials and a final electronic signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the electronically annotated IDS is mailed to applicant and the annotated image is retained in the Image File Wrapper (IFW).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English reference handling in IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in a non-English language that complies with IDS requirements will be considered in view of the concise explanation submitted and insofar as it is understood on its face (e.g., drawings, chemical formulas). The examiner is not required to have the information translated unless necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's consideration is presumed only to what can be gleaned from the concise statement/translated portion; do not require applicant to file a translation as a threshold for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents submitted as part of applicant’s reply to an Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents (affidavits, declarations, patents, printed publications, etc.) submitted and relied on by applicant in a reply to an Office action need not satisfy 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 to be considered by the examiner; however, consideration is limited to the portion of the document relied upon as rebuttal evidence and the entirety may not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such documents need not be processed as IDS items; the record should reflect whether the evidence was considered. If applicant lists such documents on a PTO/SB/08A/08B but has not complied with 1.97(e) or paid the fee under 1.17(p), the examiner may indicate the teachings relied on have been considered but line through the IDS entries and inform applicant of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information printed on the patent from IDS/Examiner citations
rubrics_metrics.description: A citation listed on form PTO/SB/08A and 08B and considered by the examiner will be printed on the patent. Examiner-cited references listed on form PTO-892 will be distinguished (marked with an asterisk). If a citation is listed multiple places it will appear only once on the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting requirements for printing: each item on a single line, double-spaced lines, uniform format. Applicants may avoid printing pending U.S. application numbers on the patent by listing them on other than a PTO/SB/08A/08B format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models, exhibits, and specimens generally not admitted
rubrics_metrics.description: A model, exhibit, or specimen is normally not admitted as part of the application, although it may be required in the prosecution of the application (37 CFR 1.91 and 1.93; MPEP § 608.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such items are needed during prosecution, they will be handled according to specific MPEP rules for handling models/exhibits/specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary classification requested from applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants are requested to include a preliminary classification on newly filed patent applications (preferably class and subclass designations) identified in the transmittal letter or in the application data sheet after the title of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "Proposed Class 2, subclass 129." Providing preliminary classification assists the Office in processing and routing the application.
